topics.label: Lecture opening and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture scope and outlines the key learning outcomes regarding cancer evolution and microenvironmental influences.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic drivers of clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer progresses through Darwinian selection of mutated clones and how epigenetic modifications can similarly alter cellular transcription to drive tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Stem cell hierarchies and the cell of origin in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the role of tissue stem cell hierarchies in tumor development, presenting theoretical models and experimental evidence for cancer stem cells across different malignancies.

topics.label: Microenvironmental promotion, inflammation, and stromal dependency
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental promoters, chronic inflammation, and supportive stromal interactions provide essential non-mutational signals that enable tumor initiation, stemness, and continued growth.

topics.label: Methodological approaches to studying tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the single-cell sequencing technologies, computational modeling, and spatial omics techniques used to investigate tumor evolution and cellular interactions.

topics.label: Multifactorial synthesis of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic integrates genetic mutations, epigenetic plasticity, cell of origin, and microenvironmental factors into a unified evolutionary model of malignancy.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on cancer therapy.
